speaker_role: independent counselor / essay coach (College Essay Guy, Northwestern alum, says he has spoken with admissions readers)
commercial_incentive: Sells one-on-one coaching and resources via CollegeEssayGuy.com; mentioned briefly at the end.
key_insights: Do not base the essay on size, location, weather, or rankings; schools' own prompts say readers are tired of these and they reveal nothing about fit.
Vague emotional statements (I just felt it on campus), repeating brochure language, and famous traditions are weak; a Google search of traditions tells you what to leave out.
The essay is about why you and the school match, not a tribute to the school; formula is a school-specific detail plus how it connects to you.
Strong research technique: find a course syllabus in your department of interest and reference what is actually taught; capitalized proper nouns in your draft signal real research.
Three approaches: many solid reasons (10-15 researched), three to five unique offerings that set the school apart, or one core value with a story; the second suits short word counts.
Undecided applicants can still write specifics by naming core values and school resources that fit an exploratory approach, rather than claiming a major.
Keep the hook very short (about 40 words in his example) and get to school-specific content fast.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Suggests at least an hour of research, and 10 to 15 reasons for the basic approach.
Says why-us essays vary in length from 150 to 250 to 650 words depending on the school.
Says wrong school name in the essay leads to automatic rejection per readers he has spoken to.
Notes Johns Hopkins had no why-us essay at the time of recording (dated).
notable_or_distinctive: Concrete, repeatable method (syllabus lookup, capital-letter scan, bolding reasons) plus annotated real sample essays.
reliability_notes: Some school prompts and policies cited are dated (5 years old); reader claims are secondhand and captions have minor garbling.
